changes.title: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler adds 589 new API actions and event bus targets
changes.detail: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler expands its AWS SDK integrations with 589 new API actions across 81 AWS services, and adds templated targets for the enhanced EventBridge Custom event bus. You can now schedule direct invocations of a broader set of AWS services without writing custom integration code. EventBridge Scheduler is a serverless scheduler that allows you to create, run, and manage billions of scheduled events and tasks across more than 270 AWS services, without provisioning or managing the underlying infrastructure. changes.title: Amazon EventBridge Custom event bus now supports Webhook Events
changes.detail: Amazon EventBridge now supports Webhook Events for the enhanced Custom event bus, so SaaS applications, AI agents, and custom integrations can send events to a bus over HTTPS. You no longer need to deploy and operate your own API endpoint and compute to receive webhooks and publish them to your bus. changes.title: Amazon EventBridge Custom event bus now supports Amazon MSK as a target
changes.detail: Amazon EventBridge now supports Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) as a target for the enhanced Custom event bus, so you can deliver events to Kafka topics without running your own producer. changes.title: Amazon VPC Lattice now supports CloudWatch metrics for VPC resources
changes.detail: Amazon VPC Lattice now publishes Amazon CloudWatch metrics for VPC resources. Resource owners — those who share resources via VPC Lattice — and resource consumers — those who access those shared resources — can now see TCP traffic to resources such as databases, clusters, and on-premises endpoints. Resource owners get metrics for resource gateways and resource configurations. Consumers get metrics for resource endpoints, service network endpoints, and service network VPC associations.
